slides.1.title: Madeira's Official Age and Vintage Designations
slides.1.html:
Portugal's IVBAM (the Madeira Wine, Embroidery and Handicrafts Institute) governs Madeira's official classification. Age statements (5/10/15/20… years) apply to non-vintage blends of different years, approved by an IVBAM tasting panel as having "the style of that age"; they are not a guaranteed minimum or average age.

LabelAge / ruleMethodCharacteristics
Finest / Selected / Choice Quality term — A quality term recognised by law, not an age grade; entry level
Reserva (Velho / Reserve) 5 years Estufagem / Canteiro Everyday drinking, good value
Reserva Velha / Special Reserve 10 years Mainly Canteiro Clear complexity, with varietal character beginning to show
Reserva Extra / Extra Reserve 15 years Canteiro Refined and profound, an entry point for collecting
20 / 30 / 40 / 50 years Number of years stated directly Canteiro Beyond 50 years, the label gives a written description
Colheita (single vintage) At least 5 years in cask Continuous cask ageing A single harvest year, with quality approved
Frasqueira / Garrafeira ⭐ At least 20 years in cask Canteiro only Single vintage, recommended variety, quality must be outstanding

Frasqueira is Portuguese for "glass bottle" and is synonymous with top Madeira. It requires at least 20 years of Canteiro ageing, is of the highest quality, and can continue to age for 50–100 years.
slides.2.title: Why Can Madeira Age for a Century? The Triple Protection Mechanism
slides.2.html:
Madeira is the longest-lived wine in the world, thanks to three mutually reinforcing protective mechanisms:

1️⃣ Full oxidation (already stable)

  • The Estufagem / Canteiro methods oxidise the wine fully, converting all compounds prone to spoilage
  • A wine that is "fully oxidised" will not deteriorate further through contact with oxygen
  • An analogy: once iron has completely rusted it will not rust any more

2️⃣ High alcohol (17–22%)

  • High alcohol inhibits all microbial activity (acetic acid bacteria, lactic acid bacteria, wild yeasts)
  • Above 18%, no microorganism can survive

3️⃣ High acidity

  • Madeira's natural acidity is extremely high (pH 3.0–3.2), inhibiting bacteria
  • It also provides a supporting backbone, so the wine stays lively and shows no sign of age even after a century

🏆 Documented Century-Old Madeira

  • Blandy's 1900 Vintage Malmsey: harvested in 1900, still available to buy and drink, and in astonishing condition
slides.3.question: What is the minimum ageing requirement for Madeira's highest grade, "Frasqueira (Vintage)"?
slides.3.options.2: At least 20 years of ageing by the natural Canteiro method
slides.3.options.3: At least 2 years of heating by Estufagem
slides.3.explanation: Frasqueira (Vintage Madeira) is Madeira's highest grade. It must use the natural Canteiro method (not industrial Estufagem), be aged in oak casks for at least 20 years, and be a single vintage. After bottling it can continue to age for 50–100 years or more.
slides.4.question: What does the triple protection mechanism that lets Madeira age for a century consist of?
slides.4.options.0: Low alcohol + low sugar + low temperature
slides.4.options.1: Full oxidation (already stable) + high alcohol (17–22%) + high acidity
slides.4.options.3: Low yields + special varieties + hand harvesting
slides.4.explanation: The secret of Madeira's century-long ageing lies in triple protection: ① full oxidation (the Estufagem/Canteiro methods leave the wine completely stable, no longer deteriorating through oxygen); ② high alcohol (17–22%, inhibiting all microorganisms); ③ high acidity (pH 3.0–3.2, inhibiting bacteria and maintaining structural vitality). Together they make it the longest-lived wine in the world.
slides.5.title: Madeira Labelling and Regulations: Supplementary Notes
slides.5.html:
A few legal details of Madeira that are easily overlooked:

  • When a grape variety is named on the label, the wine must contain ≥ 85% of that variety; Tinta Negra makes up about 80–85% of Madeira's output yet is not one of the four noble varieties, and inexpensive wines without a variety on the label are mostly based on it
  • Estufagem: heated to about 45–50°C and held for 3 months, then rested for ≥ 90 days before going into cask; it may not be released until 2 years after harvest. The gentler armazéns de calor (heated warehouses) heat at lower temperatures for up to about 1 year
  • Canteiro: ≥ 2 years in cask (attics, south-facing windows and other natural heat sources), and only bottled after ≥ 3 years; top wines may spend more than 20 years in cask
  • Colheita and Frasqueira both require ≥ 85% of grapes from the stated vintage; Frasqueira requires ≥ 20 years in cask and a further ≥ 2 years in bottle before release
  • Non-vintage blends: Rainwater (popular in the US market, mainly Tinta Negra, lightly sweet and light, youngest wine ≥ 3 years), Finest / Choice (3–5 years), Reserva (5–10 years), Special Reserve (10–15 years), Extra Reserve (15–20 years)
  • Solera labelling (fractional blending) has been banned since Portugal joined the EU, and only older wines made before the ban remain on the market

Based on material compiled around 2012; for details, the current IVBAM regulations prevail.
